This made the walker treat non-If branches (e.g. a single-statement Block) as if they were nested If nodes, so it unconditionally accessed `branch.cond.fast`, crashing with AttributeError on Block objects. answer.summary: Fixed inverted class check in Interp._if_chain: changed `branch.__class__ is not A.If` to `branch.__class__ is A.If` so the else-if fast-path chain-walk only dereferences `branch.cond` when branch really is an If node, matching the correct logic already used in `_if_inline`.

answer.root_cause: In interp.py's compile-time handler for A.If, the guard used a double negation `if not not (cf and tf and ef): return False`, which inverted the intended check. It bailed out (returned False, meaning 'fall back / cannot compile') precisely when cf, tf, ef all successfully compiled, and instead proceeded to build f_if/d_if when one of them was falsy (e.g. False from a failed sub()). This let a non-callable (e.g. plain bool) leak into ef, causing `branch = ef(env)` to raise `TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable`.
answer.summary: Fixed the inverted guard in the If-node fast-path compiler: changed `if not not (cf and tf and ef): return False` to `if not (cf and tf and ef): return False`, restoring the correct fallback behavior when any sub-expression fails to compile, and allowing normal compilation to proceed when all three succeed.
